subject: Reserved commit duration & tiered GPU-pool phasing — Neon Labs
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex@neonlabs.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Neon Labs Procurement <procurement@neonlabs.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated reserved commit question — term flexibility and phasing

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput numbers looked promising. We're digging into economics with procurement and need to understand a few things before we move to a commercial term:

- Term options: Neon is evaluating 12/24/36 month reserved commits. For our financial model we need to know how pricing and discounts scale by term (especially effective $/token and any GPU-hour guarantees).
- Phased start: We will initially route a small slice of traffic (about 10% of the committed QPS) for 6-8 weeks for validation. Can we ramp the guaranteed pool over a 6–12 week window and only be billed at full committed rate once the full pool is active?
- Burst and overage: What are burst policies — can Neon burst above committed throughput (to a shared pool) and how are overage tokens billed?
- GPU sizing guidance: Based on the usage profile I shared (median sequence length ~128, 10k daily concurrent requests at peak), what GPU pool size would you recommend for stable 95th percentile latency of <150ms?

Procurement will also need a short summary doc and an invoice schedule (deposit + monthly invoice). Can you point me to an illustrative quote and a rough timeline to get to a signed PO?

If easier, happy to set up a 30-min call this week.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform
Neon Labs
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@neonlabs.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved commit question — term flexibility and phasing

Hi Alex — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. I pulled together options below; attaching a short "Reserved_Commit_Tiers_v2.pdf" that lays out pricing bands and ramp mechanics.

TL;DR: We support 12/24/36 month terms with stepped effective discounts; we can accommodate a phased activation window and a provisional billing approach during the validation period.

Options (illustrative):
- 12-month: baseline price, no upfront discount, 5% discount on additional committed months beyond month 6.
- 24-month: ~12% effective discount vs 12-month; 50% of the first month as an upfront deposit, monthly invoicing thereafter.
- 36-month: ~20% effective discount vs 12-month; 25% upfront deposit option to reduce monthly rates further.

Phased start / ramping:
- We can define an activation window (6–12 weeks) during which Neon pays a staged fraction of the committed capacity: e.g., first 2 weeks 25% of committed rate, weeks 3–6 50%, weeks 7–12 75%, then full at final activation.
- Billing during the window will reflect staged committed capacity; usage above the staged commitment will be billed as overage at the negotiated overage rate (lower than on-demand). At the end of the activation window you can choose to lock to the final committed tier or extend staging (one-time extension allowed).

Burst and overage:
- Burst to shared pool: allowed up to a negotiated burst ceiling. Overage tokens billed at the overage rate in the quote (we can cap monthly overage charges if desired).

GPU sizing guidance (based on your profile):
- Recommended starting pool: 8 x A100-class equivalents (or equivalent vGPU mix) to hit 95th <150ms at your stated concurrency with batching.
- If you enable prefix KV caching and conservative batching (max batch 32), we estimate required GPU-hours to align to your daily peak. We will include a concrete sizing appendix in the quote if you share a 7-day sample trace or more granularity.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus will prepare an itemized commercial quote (term-by-term) and include a sample activation schedule and deposit options.
2) Karthik will flag any suggested SLA/burst guardrails for the quote.
3) If Neon confirms a preferred term (e.g., 24 months) we'll prepare a DocuSign-ready SOW + invoice schedule for procurement.

Attached: reserved_commit_tiers_v2.pdf (pricing bands + ramp examples)
Also attaching: neon_requirements_matrix.xlsx (your initial profile with our sizing notes).

Would you be available for a quick sync tomorrow at 11:00 AM PT?

Best,
Priya Natarajan

Alex / Priya — quick note from pricing/ops:

- I've attached the internal tier doc for transparency (Reserved_Commit_Tiers_v2.pdf). For Neon I recommend we lead with the 24-month band — it gives Neon meaningful savings and keeps us flexible on GPU pool sizing during the activation window.
- SLA / throughput guarantee: we'll commit to a minimum sustained throughput per the quote (tokens/sec) with a 95th-percentile latency SLO. For breaches that are our fault we offer service credits (structured by % downtime or latency miss) — we should agree on the exact SLO language before final SOW.
- Burst policy: allow bursts to shared pool with an agreed monthly cap; overages billed at the overage rate. If Neon expects frequent bursts we should include burst-reserve add-on (priced).
- Procurement-friendly invoice cadence: deposit (25% or 50% depending on term) + monthly invoicing; we can also do quarterly invoicing for enterprise procurement.

I'll draft the quote and include two activation schedules (6-week aggressive, 12-week conservative) so procurement can choose. Priya — happy for you to push DocuSign once Neon signals 24-month preferred.

—Marcus

Thanks Priya and Marcus — this is helpful. Procurement reviewed and the internal preference is to proceed with a 24-month reserved commit with the 12-week conservative activation window. A few items to confirm before we loop legal:

1) Can Redwood set the deposit at 30% for 24-months instead of 50%? That helps our cashflow.
2) Please include a hard cap on monthly burst overage charges (we propose a 20% cap of committed spend).
3) We need the SOC2 appendix and the audit contact included in the SOW.

If you can incorporate those changes into the DocuSign SOW, procurement will circulate within 48 hours and we should be able to issue a PO within 7 business days.

Alex
